style: Hand-drawn 2D cartoon illustration for a YouTube history explainer. Simple stick-figure people: large round plain white heads, thin black stick arms and legs, sleepy half-closed eyes with heavy eyelids and tiny pupils, small simple mouths, messy brown hair, orange leopard-print one-shoulder caveman tunics (Neanderthals: tan skin, heavy brow, long brown hair, brown fur tunic). Thick clean black ink outlines, flat bright colors with soft painterly shading, detailed cartoon background. Funny, gentle, not gory. 16:9 widescreen. Absolutely no text, letters, captions or watermark in the image.

shots.p: Inside a dark cave lit by a campfire, a caveman wakes up on a fur bed holding his swollen cheek, wincing in pain.
shots.line: Imagine waking up with a toothache.

shots.p: Close-up of the caveman's face, eyes squeezed shut in pain, red throbbing glow lines around his swollen cheek, a tiny red heart pulsing beside him.
shots.line: Not a little one. The kind that throbs every time your heart beats.

shots.p: A worried caveman standing alone on an empty savanna at dawn, looking around, nobody to help.
shots.line: Now imagine there is no dentist.

shots.p: Split comic panel: a modern toothbrush and a bottle of pills floating in the sky with big red X marks over them, a confused caveman looking up at them.
shots.line: No toothbrush. No painkillers.

shots.p: A caveman scratching his head with a giant question mark above him, staring at a cartoon tooth he holds in his palm.
shots.line: Nobody even knows what tooth decay is.

shots.p: Thumbnail-style hero shot: a caveman holding his swollen cheek in pain in front of a cave with a campfire, mountains behind, dramatic but funny.
shots.line: So what did ancient humans actually do about their teeth?

shots.p: A group of cavemen sitting around a campfire looking surprisingly calm and content, one smiling widely showing healthy teeth.
shots.line: Surprisingly, a lot more than you'd think.

shots.p: Cartoon archaeologist with a magnifying glass examining an ancient human skull's teeth on a desk, glowing clues around the teeth.
shots.line: And a lot of the evidence is still stuck to their teeth today.

shots.p: Sunny savanna with acacia trees, a happy family of cavemen walking with spears, blue sky with fluffy clouds.
shots.line: Let's start with the good news.

shots.p: A caveman grinning proudly at the viewer, showing a full set of shiny healthy white teeth that sparkle.
shots.line: For most of human history, cavities were actually pretty rare.

shots.p: Giant cartoon molar tooth with cute green bacteria monsters with tiny teeth munching on sugar cubes and bread crumbs on its surface.
shots.line: Cavities happen when bacteria in your mouth feed on sugars and starches,

shots.p: The giant cartoon molar now has a dark brown hole eaten into its top, acid drops dripping, the bacteria looking smug.
shots.line: and leave behind acid that slowly eats into your teeth.

shots.p: Cavemen eating roasted meat and wild roots around a fire, no bread, no sweets in sight.
shots.line: And for a very long time, people just didn't eat much of that.

shots.p: A long neat row of cartoon ancient teeth on a museum table, almost all perfectly healthy, only one or two with small dark spots.
shots.line: Studies of hunter-gatherer teeth usually find decay in somewhere between zero and about fourteen percent of teeth.

shots.p: A caveman sitting on a rock chewing a tough root, wincing slightly.
shots.line: But their food came with a different problem.

shots.p: Close-up of a caveman biting into a sandy, gritty root, little sand grains flying around his mouth.
shots.line: It was tough, and it was full of grit and sand.

shots.p: Three cartoon teeth in a row showing wear over time: sharp, a bit flat, completely flat and ground down.
shots.line: Chewing it day after day slowly wore their teeth down.

shots.p: A cartoon tooth with a dark cavity, crossed out with a big red X.
shots.line: So for most of our history, the big problem wasn't holes in teeth.

shots.p: Three cartoon teeth side by side: one worn flat, one chipped at the corner, one with a crack running down it.
shots.line: It was teeth that were worn, chipped and cracked.

shots.p: A caveman after a big meal, a stringy piece of meat stuck between his front teeth, annoyed expression.
shots.line: And when something got stuck between their teeth?

shots.p: A modern office worker stick figure in a blue shirt using a toothpick after lunch at a desk.
shots.line: They did what you might have done after lunch today.

shots.p: The caveman happily picking his teeth with a thin wooden twig, relieved expression.
shots.line: They grabbed a toothpick.

shots.p: Extreme close-up diagram of two fossil teeth side by side with a small smooth groove worn between them.
shots.line: Scientists have found tiny grooves on fossil teeth,

shots.p: A grass stem being pushed back and forth between two cartoon teeth, motion lines showing repetition.
shots.line: worn in by sticks or grass stems being pushed between the teeth again and again.

shots.p: An early human ancestor, Homo habilis: smaller, hairy, ape-like stick figure with a hairy head, picking teeth with a grass stem on an ancient African plain.
shots.line: Some of these toothpick grooves go back close to two million years,

shots.p: Timeline illustration: a long winding path across the savanna going back into the distance, tiny early humans along it.
shots.line: to early human species like Homo habilis.

shots.p: Forested hills of Croatia with a rocky cave entrance, a Neanderthal standing outside holding his jaw.
shots.line: But one Neanderthal from Krapina, in what is now Croatia, takes this further.

shots.p: The Neanderthal sitting in the cave, peering into a polished stone reflection at his crooked tooth.
shots.line: Around a hundred and thirty thousand years ago, this person had a tooth growing in crooked,

shots.p: Cartoon x-ray style view of a jaw with one tooth growing in sideways and crooked, red pain lines around it.
shots.line: and it was very likely painful.

shots.p: Close-up of a cartoon Neanderthal jaw with six small toothpick grooves highlighted in yellow around the crooked tooth.
shots.line: Their teeth show six toothpick grooves around the problem area, plus scratches and chips.

shots.p: The Neanderthal poking at his crooked tooth with a twig, again and again, sweat drop, determined face.
shots.line: It looks like they were poking at it, over and over, trying to ease the pain.

shots.p: A modern dentist's chair glowing in a spotlight, next to it a Neanderthal with a twig, comparing the two.
shots.line: It's not dentistry the way we know it.

shots.p: The Neanderthal smiling with relief, holding the twig like a trophy, warm cave firelight.
shots.line: But it may be one of the earliest signs of someone trying to treat their own toothache.

shots.p: A big cave entrance in green Spanish hills, a Neanderthal standing in front of it.
shots.line: Then there's a Neanderthal from El Sidrón cave, in Spain.

shots.p: A cartoon scientist stick figure in a white lab coat and goggles carefully scraping hardened yellow plaque off an ancient tooth with a tiny tool.
shots.line: Scientists took the hardened plaque from this individual's teeth,

shots.p: A glowing DNA double helix emerging from a tooth under a microscope in a modern lab.
shots.line: and read the ancient DNA trapped inside it.

shots.p: The Neanderthal holding his swollen cheek, a red throbbing abscess glow on his jaw.
shots.line: This Neanderthal had a painful dental abscess.

shots.p: A tall green poplar tree by a river, the Neanderthal looking up at it.
shots.line: And in the plaque was DNA from poplar,

shots.p: The Neanderthal chewing on poplar bark, a dotted arrow linking the bark to a modern aspirin pill floating beside it.
shots.line: a tree that contains salicylic acid, the natural pain reliever behind aspirin.

shots.p: Green-blue fuzzy Penicillium mold growing on old bread, magnified, cute and not gross.
shots.line: There were also traces of Penicillium,

shots.p: A small glass vial of penicillin next to a petri dish of mold in a cartoon lab.
shots.line: the same group of molds that penicillin comes from.

shots.p: The Neanderthal sitting by a campfire chewing a twig, a thought bubble with a poplar leaf and a question mark.
shots.line: So was this Neanderthal chewing poplar on purpose, to dull the pain?

shots.p: The cartoon scientist in a lab coat shrugging with both hands up next to a microscope.
shots.line: The researchers say they can't prove it.

shots.p: The Neanderthal and the scientist looking at each other with matching puzzled expressions.
shots.line: But it's hard not to wonder.

shots.p: Snowy Alps of northern Italy with pine trees and a valley, a hunter-gatherer in furs walking with a spear.
shots.line: Now jump forward to about fourteen thousand years ago,

shots.p: Wide view of the northern Italian mountains, a small rock shelter under a huge overhanging cliff.
shots.line: in the mountains of northern Italy.

shots.p: A hunter-gatherer sitting under the rock overhang of a rock shelter, holding his jaw in pain.
shots.line: A hunter-gatherer buried at a rock shelter called Villabruna

shots.p: Cartoon cross-section of a back molar with a large dark cavity in the top.
shots.line: had a large cavity in one of his back molars.

shots.p: Microscope view: the cavity's walls covered in tiny parallel scratch marks.
shots.line: Under a microscope, that cavity is covered in tiny scratches.

shots.p: A sharp pointed piece of grey flint held in a stick-figure hand, glinting.
shots.line: They match marks made by a pointed piece of flint,

shots.p: A friend carefully scratching inside the sitting man's open mouth with a pointed flint, the patient gripping a rock with wide eyes.
shots.line: used to scratch and lever out the rotten part of the tooth, while he was still alive.

shots.p: The patient sitting on a rock looking terrified and brave at the same time, tears in eyes, friend holding the flint.
shots.line: No numbing. No drill.

shots.p: Heroic shot of the patient giving a shaky thumbs up, sweat drops, mountains behind.
shots.line: Just a sharp stone, and a lot of courage.

shots.p: Rolling Tuscan hills near Lucca with a small stone shelter, a hunter-gatherer woman sitting outside.
shots.line: About a thousand years later, someone near Lucca, also in Italy, went a step further.

shots.p: Close-up of two cartoon upper front teeth with scraped-out holes.
shots.line: Two of this person's front teeth had been scraped out,

shots.p: A small clay pot of black sticky tar, plant fibers beside it, a hand pressing the tar into the tooth holes.
shots.line: and the holes were packed with bitumen, a sticky natural tar, mixed with plant fibers and possibly hair.

shots.p: A cartoon front tooth with a neat black tar filling, shining proudly.
shots.line: In other words, it's one of the earliest fillings we know of.

shots.p: A sunrise over a wide plain, stick-figure people looking at the horizon in awe, a big change coming.
shots.line: And then, everything changed.

shots.p: Early farmers planting and harvesting golden wheat fields next to round mud huts.
shots.line: Around ten thousand years ago, people in several parts of the world started farming.

shots.p: A table with bowls of porridge, flat bread and piles of grain.
shots.line: Grains. Porridge. Bread.

shots.p: A caveman family happily eating sticky porridge every day, porridge on their faces.
shots.line: Starchy, sticky food, every single day.

shots.p: Cute green bacteria monsters cheering and partying on top of a pile of bread and porridge.
shots.line: Perfect food for the bacteria that cause cavities.

shots.p: Rocky warm hills of Morocco with oak trees, a cave entrance in the hillside.
shots.line: Actually, one group got there early.

shots.p: Hunter-gatherers sitting around piles of acorns, cracking and eating them.
shots.line: At Taforalt, in Morocco, about fifteen thousand years ago, hunter-gatherers ate a lot of acorns.

shots.p: A row of cavemen grimacing and holding their cheeks, all with toothaches.
shots.line: And almost every adult there had cavities.

shots.p: A busy prehistoric village with more people holding their jaws, a line forming outside one hut.
shots.line: More cavities meant more dentistry.

shots.p: Mud-brick village of Mehrgarh on a dry plain with mountains behind, villagers at work.
shots.line: At Mehrgarh, in what is now Pakistan, people who lived around seven and a half to nine thousand years ago

shots.p: Two cartoon molars, each with a small round drilled hole in the top.
shots.line: had holes drilled into their molars.

shots.p: A villager operating a bow drill with a flint tip, the bow moving back and forth, motion lines.
shots.line: Researchers think the tool was a bow drill tipped with flint.

shots.p: The bow drill touching a tooth, a sand timer beside it showing less than a minute.
shots.line: In tests, a drill like that could cut into tooth enamel in under a minute.

shots.p: A nervous patient sitting very still with mouth open, a villager approaching with a bow drill.
shots.line: And these holes weren't made after death.

shots.p: The patient with wide shocked eyes, very much alive, gripping the seat.
shots.line: The patients were alive.

shots.p: A row of three cartoon molars, two of them with drilled holes, from the same person.
shots.line: Some of them even had more than one tooth drilled.

shots.p: Green hills and karst limestone of Slovenia, a young man walking near a cave.
shots.line: Then, about sixty-five hundred years ago, in what is now Slovenia,

shots.p: Close-up of a pointy canine tooth with a crack running down it.
shots.line: a man in his twenties had a cracked canine tooth.

shots.p: A honeycomb dripping golden beeswax, a cartoon bee buzzing, a hand pressing wax into the cracked canine.
shots.line: Someone filled the crack with beeswax.

shots.p: The young man chewing happily with no pain, beeswax filling glowing gold on his tooth.
shots.line: It may have been to stop the pain when he chewed.

shots.p: The cartoon scientist examining the old jaw with a magnifying glass, a question mark above her head.
shots.line: Although scientists can't completely rule out that the wax was added after he died.

shots.p: Night scene: cavemen sitting around a crackling campfire under the stars and a crescent moon.
shots.line: So, did ancient humans take care of their teeth?

shots.p: A toothbrush, dental floss and a calendar with a checkup date floating above the campfire, all crossed out.
shots.line: Not the way we do. No brushing twice a day. No floss. No checkups.

shots.p: Collage: a twig toothpick, a sharp flint and a bow drill arranged together like tools on a workbench.
shots.line: But they picked at them, scraped out the rot with stone,

shots.p: A pot of black tar and a honeycomb side by side with a cartoon tooth between them.
shots.line: drilled with flint, and plugged the holes with tar and wax.

shots.p: A caveman with a big question mark, eyebrows raised, curious expression.
shots.line: And the strangest part?

shots.p: A modern city skyline rising from wheat fields, showing how farming led to modern life.
shots.line: Their biggest tooth problem came from the very thing that made modern life possible.

shots.p: A single golden wheat stalk in a spotlight, dramatic.
shots.line: Farming.

shots.p: A modern stick-figure patient nervously sitting in a bright modern dentist's chair, dentist in a white coat smiling.
shots.line: So next time you're sitting in a dentist's chair, remember.

shots.p: The modern patient relaxing and smiling, giving a thumbs up in the comfy dentist chair.
shots.line: It could be a lot worse.

shots.p: A caveman popping up next to the modern dentist chair holding a sharp flint, grinning, the patient horrified.
shots.line: It could be a sharp rock.

shots.p: A cheerful caveman waving goodbye on the sunny savanna with a campfire.
